subject: Intermittent generation stalls on ember-3b — timeline, mitigation, and next steps
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@nexahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: production errors from ember-3b (09/04)

Marcus —

We're seeing a steady stream of 5xx / "generation stall" errors from requests routed to ember-3b since ~07:55 UTC. Affected endpoints are our patient-summary and note-generation routes (high QPS windows). Errors show up as: 

- 500 internal
- 504 timeout: token generation stalled after first 2–3 tokens

Attached is a short CSV with timestamps and request IDs. Impact: a ~15% drop in success rate, retries are spiking. Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or something in our integration? We briefly switched to a fallback model this morning which reduced errors.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Platform Lead, Nexa Health

Attachment: nexa-impact-log-snippet-0904.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 08:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: production errors from ember-3b (09/04)

Priya —

Thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. I'm opening an incident and looping in SRE & the model ops team. Initial ask: could you forward a few of the raw request IDs (x-request-id header) showing 504s? That'll let us pull traces.

What we know so far:
- Multiple customers are reporting increased stall / 5xx for ember-3b starting ~07:40–08:00 UTC.
- Fallback to an alternative model reduces errors (good temporary mitigation).

Short timeline: we will collect traces, check model node health and recent kernel/quantization rollouts, and test an immediate routing change to avoid ember-3b variants that hit the anomaly. I'll update you within 90 minutes.

—Marcus

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 09:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: production errors from ember-3b (09/04)

Team —

Quick update from ops after correlating traces with the node metrics:
- Root symptom: persistent KV cache thrashing on a subset of ember-3b nodes serving long contexts. We see repeated cache evictions + elevated GPU memory churn.
- Trigger: a scheduled quantization kernel rollout (v3.4.1) completed 07:30 UTC across the ember-3b pool; a small subset (approx 9%) of nodes show regressions under long-prefix traffic leading to stalls.
- Impact window: 07:40–08:40 UTC (matches customer reports).

Immediate mitigations performed (08:40–08:50 UTC):
- Rolled back the v3.4.1 kernel on the affected node pool to v3.4.0.
- Automated routing rule applied to shift pod traffic away from the small cohort while rollback completed.
- Warm restart of the affected nodes to clear KV state.

Post-mitigation status at 09:05 UTC: error rate for ember-3b down to baseline; Nexa's fallback showed restored success while we applied the rollback.

Attachments: I exported a 30s trace sample and a small text dump of the kernel error logs — see ember3b-sample-trace-20280904.txt attached.

Next steps:
1) Full node-level audit (will run overnight) to identify root kernel change that regressed under long-prefix sequences.
2) Re-run quantization rollout in canary with longer-context traffic shaping.
3) Re-run Nexa's exact production prompt set in dedicated canary to validate.

I'll draft a short postmortem and proposed action items once audit completes.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Postmortem: ember-3b stall regression (09/04) — findings and actions

Priya —

Apologies for the delay — we validated the audit and I wanted to give you a concise postmortem and our planned follow-ups. Summary for Nexa Health:

What happened
- A quantization kernel update (v3.4.1) deployed to ember-3b nodes introduced a performance regression under long-prefix generation traffic, causing repeated KV cache flushes and subsequent token-generation stalls for ~9% of the node cohort between 07:40–08:40 UTC on 2028-09-04.

Impact
- Nexa Health: ~15% increase in request failures for note-generation endpoints during the incident window. You mitigated user-visible errors by switching to a fallback model — good call.
- Cross-customer: short-lived elevated 5xxs for customers with long-context workloads.

Root cause
- A code-path in the v3.4.1 kernel changed LRU handling for the KV cache under quantized execution paths; this caused higher eviction churn and unexpected blocking during certain memory compaction cycles. Under long contexts, token generation would sometimes stall waiting on stale KV access.

Immediate fixes applied
- Rolled back kernel to v3.4.0 for affected pool (08:45 UTC).
- Applied routing avoidance for affected nodes during rollback.
- Warm restarts to flush KV caches and force a consistent runtime state.

Longer-term actions (owner, ETA)
- Model ops: add longer-context traffic to quantization canary tests and add a KV-thrash detector to rollout healthchecks (Evelyn Hart, ETA: 2028-09-11).
- Runtime: patch LRU edge-case in quantized kernel to prevent blocking on compaction (Runtime Eng, Dylan Brooks owner for validation, ETA: 2028-09-18).
- Platform: add automated automated fallbacks from ember-3b -> ember-3b-lite when KV-thrash signals exceed threshold (Platform Eng, ETA: 2028-09-21).

What we need from Nexa (optional)
- A sample set of 10 anonymized requests that exercise your long-context prompt patterns (you offered earlier). We'll use those in canary verification. If you prefer, we can run the same set from a dedicated Nexa canary token.

Status
- As of 09/04 09:05 UTC, error rates returned to baseline. The targeted validation run on 09/05 showed no recurrence in our canary. We will keep Nexa's fallback as a safety window until the kernel fix is validated.

Attachment: ember3b-sample-trace-20280904.txt (ops trace), nexa-impact-log-snippet-0904.csv (from Nexa)

If you'd like a short joint postmortem call, I'm available tomorrow 10:00–12:00 PDT. Otherwise we'll keep you updated on the engineering work and mark once the runtime patch is live.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
